infosec.title: Virtualization security: attack layers and misconfiguration impact

In a separate case, The Gentlemen group found plaintext Proxmox root credentials in an admin's notes. It used the VNC websocket API to encrypt the entire cluster, with neither attack requiring a VM escape. Defenders should give monitoring tools dedicated least-privilege identities, vault unique per-host credentials, keep ESXi SSH off behind vCenter Lockdown Mode, and alert on execInstalledOnly or Secure Boot changes.

infosec.title: The attack chain behind the v1.107.0 LiteLLM release
infosec.summary: An admin key for LiteLLM's internal Agent Platform was committed to a public repo on May 27 and removed hours later but never revoked, and on October 10 an attacker used it to pull an org owner's unscoped GitHub CLI token from the platform API. With that token and two maintainer tokens stolen through CI workflows, the attacker overrode branch protection, built from a lookalike Berri-AI fork, and published poisoned wheels and images that stayed up for about two hours. Defenders should revoke any key that was ever committed, keep unscoped CLI tokens out of automation, and alert on branch protection overrides and deleted workflow runs.

infosec.title: Secure Code Benchmark Finds Top Coding Agents Write Secure Code Only 25% of the Time

Agents often added local defenses like bounds checks but almost never secured SSRF or information exposure, which depend on policies the spec never stated, and a one-line security reminder raised joint pass rates by 15 to 21 points for three of the four models retested. Pooled together, the six models secured 44% of tasks, though the tests and specs were drafted with Qwen's own Qwen3.8-Max, which the authors argued did not tilt the results.

fintech.title: Remote launches Expense Cards built into EOR, bringing spend into the same system as pay
fintech.summary: Launched November 5, Remote's virtual expense cards let eligible employees pay for work purchases without advancing personal funds and waiting for reimbursement. Spending controls and transaction records connect to employment data already held in its employer-of-record platform, reducing separate reconciliation work. Availability is limited to eligible EOR customers in supported countries, with no platform or per-card charge

fintech.title: Google makes big plans for wallet
fintech.summary: Google's wallet plans extend beyond in-store payments to receipts, order tracking, refunds, and merchant offers. Google is also building constrained credentials that let third-party agents pay without exposing private data, and the company says the infrastructure already exists with Gemini and Google Pay, so product experience is now the focus. The move sets Google against Stripe's Link and agentic commerce protocols from OpenAI, Visa, and Mastercard, though the article gives no adoption figures.

fintech.title: Goldman Sachs restricted Claude Code for bankers — but made one surprising exception
fintech.summary: Goldman Sachs has pulled Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub coding tools from bankers and traders for engineering work, while exempting its quantitative strats. The bank weighs productivity gains against potential risks when deciding who keeps AI tools.

fintech.title: Marqeta CEO says cards remain one of the strongest tools for customer engagement
fintech.summary: Marqeta CEO Mike Milotich says large companies are increasingly using card products and embedded finance to increase customer engagement and drive usage of their core platforms. Marqeta is positioning itself as the infrastructure layer for these programs, bundling card issuing, payments, and newer capabilities such as stablecoin-backed cards, while Q3 processing volume rose 29% to $126.5 billion and revenue increased 8% to $176.2 million.

fintech.title: BMO Turns to Agentic AI to Resolve Card Issues
fintech.summary: BMO's November 6 launch gives Canadian contact-centre employees AI tools that match transactions, retrieve policies, and prepare cases, reducing the work of switching between systems. The bank targets 20%–30% shorter handling times for eligible calls and automatic processing of roughly 40% of eligible credit refund requests, potentially delivering same-day credits.

fintech.title: B2B payments firm Pliant raises $80m
fintech.summary: Pliant, a global fintech specializing in highly modular B2B payment solutions, today announced an $80 million Series C funding round led by Seaya Nova and Speedinvest.

fintech.title: Fiserv doubles savings target to $1B and explores asset sales
fintech.summary: Fiserv has doubled its cost-savings target to $1 billion, already cutting about 3,000 employees and contractors.

fintech.title: KCB Tanzania integrates PayPal into mobile banking
fintech.summary: KCB Bank Tanzania has partnered with PayPal to integrate PayPal services into the KCB Mobile App, giving customers a simple, secure, and convenient way to connect to global payments directly through their banking app.

it.title: Microsoft extends undisclosed usage restrictions on Copilot Chat for enterprise users
it.summary: Microsoft is expanding usage limits on Copilot Chat for Microsoft 365 customers without separate Copilot licenses. The company hasn't disclosed the thresholds, and IT admins cannot view or override them. The rollout began November 2 for organizations with up to 2,000 seats and expands to larger enterprises November 9.

it.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
it.summary: OpenAI has reportedly secured $11 billion toward a funding round that could reach $20 billion, valuing the company at $1.25 trillion. The round remains open and is smaller than earlier fundraising ambitions, reflecting growing investor scrutiny of AI infrastructure spending and future profitability.

it.title: GPT-6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
it.summary: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized AI model designed for authorized cybersecurity tasks such as vulnerability discovery and patch validation. The model features specialized post-training and safety guardrails designed to ensure it adheres strictly to authorized scopes and rules of engagement. It is currently restricted to approved customers participating in OpenAI's Daybreak Red program.

it.title: Defense in Depth, Rebuilt for Machine Speed
it.summary: AI tools make exploitation significantly cheaper and faster. Traditional reliance on slow human patching is no longer viable for protecting systems. Instead, the security industry should adopt machine-speed defenses such as removing exposure from the open internet, network segmentation, virtual patching, and moving toward memory-safe code, alongside robust and verified backups.

it.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
it.summary: Ramp's transaction data shows that AI token spending grew just 1.5% across August and September, despite continued increases in usage. Lower model prices, enterprise discounts, and more efficient deployments are allowing companies to consume more AI without proportionately increasing budgets. Spending growth accelerated again in October, but pricing pressure remains.

it.title: In the era of AI, we are all buying technology wrong
it.summary: Traditional enterprise procurement often focuses on product specifications and discounts rather than business outcomes. Rigid RFPs and multiyear AI commitments can increase costs and limit flexibility. Use smaller proof-of-value exercises, outcome-based evaluation, and contracts aligned with how quickly technology evolves.

it.title: Give business teams building power without breaking IT governance
it.summary: Business teams want custom software now, but AI builders can create massive compliance overhead. Retool provides a centralized operational canvas where teams build business apps at AI speed (in Retool, or elsewhere) while IT retains complete visibility, database connection pooling, and SOC 2-compliant controls. Start building in Retool today .

it.title: More visibility and control over Claude Enterprise for security teams
it.summary: Anthropic has announced new enterprise security updates for Claude, including a security center for configuration reviews, inference hooks for data loss prevention integration, centralized management through a parent admin console, and access controls like remote member sign-out and EDR sensor support. These features are designed to give security teams greater visibility and control over how organization data and devices interact with Claude. Many of these updates are currently available in beta or general release.

it.title: Snowflake CoCo for Excel and Google Sheets: Governed AI
it.summary: Snowflake has announced the public preview of Snowflake CoCo for Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets, a coding agent designed to let business users interact with data using natural language. The tool orchestrates direct-to-sheet data transfers while maintaining enterprise governance, utilizing Snowflake's access controls, semantic views, and scalable virtual warehouses to build native formulas, pivot tables, and visualizations.

it.title: Google announces $17bn data center campus in Cheyenne, Wyoming
it.summary: Google has announced a $17 billion investment in its first Wyoming data center, taking over a campus previously developed by Crusoe. The project will use natural-gas-powered fuel cells, carbon capture technology, and air cooling. The development highlights the growing importance of power availability in hyperscale infrastructure expansion.

it.title: OpenAI buys tiny software developer to improve Codex
it.summary: OpenAI is acquiring Pierre Computer Company to integrate its Code.Storage Git infrastructure into Codex. Pierre's technology and open-source libraries already support Codex, and the acquisition aims to improve how human developers and AI coding agents work simultaneously across software repositories.

it.title: Playmobil owner to enter data center market with new facility in Dietenhofen, Germany
it.summary: The company behind Playmobil toys plans to transform a former German manufacturing facility into a data center campus with up to 100MW of initial power demand. The proposed project, operating under a new Playmobil digital division, would serve hyperscalers, startups, and other customers, marking an unexpected move from toy manufacturing into digital infrastructure.

it.title: Wi-Fi 8 isn't about speed - but that's exactly the point
it.summary: According to Cisco Wireless CTO, the upcoming Wi-Fi 8 standard focuses on improving network predictability, reliability, and roaming performance under dense conditions rather than increasing maximum speed. The standard introduces features like Multi-AP Coordination and a Seamless Mobility Domain to better support demanding traffic patterns driven by agentic AI and connected devices. However, industry leaders note that creating standardized enterprise certification profiles will be essential to ensure consistent interoperability.

it.title: NTT Data signs 900MW fuel cell supply deal with Bloom Energy
it.summary: NTT Data has signed an agreement to deploy up to 900MW of Bloom Energy fuel cell capacity across data centers worldwide, with initial deliveries expected in 2027. The agreement reflects an increasing reliance on on-site power generation as utilities struggle to meet the electricity demands of expanding data center infrastructure.

it.title: Atlassian: Our Q1 FY27 letter to shareholders
it.summary: Reporting strong Q1 FY2027 financial results, Atlassian emphasized momentum in its System of Work, driven by expanding adoption of its Teamwork Graph, Rovo agents, and Agentic Multiplayer Protocol.

it.title: Python is de-jitted but still de-lovely
it.summary: Python is dropping its experimental native just-in-time compiler for now over maintainability concerns, while continuing to advance its developer ecosystem and language capabilities.

it.title: The CIO's trust paradox: Your team may be more honest with AI than with you
it.summary: Emerging research suggests employees may be more comfortable challenging AI than human managers in certain situations, raising new questions about leadership, psychological safety, and how organizations surface employee concerns.

it.title: Enterprises must take blame for their AI agents' mistakes, say regulators
it.summary: Four UK regulators have warned that organizations remain accountable for autonomous AI agents they deploy.

hardware.title: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation into Jensen Huang after he admits an affair with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China
hardware.summary: Huang told employees he was unfaithful and said he supports the probe, which independent directors and outside counsel will oversee, and Nvidia says he stays on as CEO. The spy allegations against Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, which is accused of smuggling $2B of chips, remain reported assessments, not proven, and China has called them unsubstantiated.

hardware.title: AST SpaceMobile is building its own reusable rocket, Blacklift, to launch its BlueBird satellites
hardware.summary: AST is building Blacklift, a 20-ton, three-stage rocket with two reusable lower stages, to launch up to five stacked BlueBirds per flight from late 2028. It sized the vehicle around its own constellation after launch delays, including a New Glenn failure, slowed deployment, though it keeps outside launch deals for 100+ satellites. The engines come from Firefly: 27 Miranda and 9 Vira for the first three rockets, plus a license to build them itself, in a deal valued above $1.3 billion.

hardware.title: Yangwang's U9 Xtreme hits 503 km/h (312.65 mph), a one-way record, on tuned rear-wing angle, damping, and tire pressure
hardware.summary: BYD's electric hypercar, driven by Marc Basseng on a closed Abu Dhabi highway, is the first production car that can accelerate past 500 km/h. Four motors make about 2,220 kW and spin to 30,000 rpm, on custom Giti semi-slick tires. After early runs topped out near 490 km/h, engineers adjusted rear-wing angle, rebound damping in the suspension software, and tire pressures.

hardware.title: Boston Dynamics' Stretch Gen 2 cuts internal cabling 81% and swaps a swerve drive in about an hour
hardware.summary: Using data from 100,000+ operating hours, Boston Dynamics redesigned its trailer-unloading robot around downtime. It cut internal cabling 81% (about half a mile of wire), switched to automotive-grade connectors, and added continuous-rotation joints that no longer hit hard stops. A full swerve drive swap drops from a day to about an hour. It unloads up to 1,000 cases per hour (varies with weight and stacking) and fast-charges to 90% in about 75 minutes.

hardware.title: Physicists used electrical noise to show electrons in a high-temperature superconductor pair up earlier than expected
hardware.summary: Superconductors carry current when electrons team up in pairs, but in cuprates (compounds containing copper in an anionic state), scientists couldn't tell if the pairs form early or just don't exist until the material gets cold enough. The team measured electrical noise, which gets louder when charge moves in pairs, and found the extra noise appearing early. That suggests the pairs are already there and are just failing to move together, which could be what limits how warm cuprates can superconduct.

hardware.title: Groq seeks a Series B at an $8B valuation, more than double August's, as it shifts from chips to inference data centers
hardware.summary: Groq, which used to build inference chips and now operates data centers selling inference capacity, is pitching investors a Series B at $8 billion before new money, versus $3.15 billion in August. Executive chairman Alex Davis criticizes rivals' reliance on debt and projects revenue up eightfold next year and $2 billion in EBITDA by 2028. The pitch comes as listed neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius sell off on debt concerns.

hardware.title: TSMC denies reports that it is planning 3D DRAM for Nvidia
hardware.summary: The Information reported that TSMC began planning 3D DRAM production, possibly by converting an existing fab, to give Nvidia a fourth memory source, but TSMC says it stays a pure-play logic foundry with no plans to make commodity memory. The engineering case against it is that 3D DRAM, which stacks memory cells vertically, is years out even for Micron, whose roadmap has at least four more planar nodes first, and TSMC has no competitive planar DRAM process to build on.

hardware.title: Omarchy 4.5 installs natively on M1 to M3 and Neo MacBooks, its first non-x86 release, built on Asahi Linux
hardware.summary: Omarchy, an Arch-based Hyprland desktop distro, shipped 4.5 with Apple Silicon as a primary target through the Omarchy M team via a dual-boot installer.

hardware.title: Six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth $11.4M vanished on a truck from Oakland to Fort Worth
hardware.summary: A truck carrying six pallets of Nvidia hardware valued at $11.4 million left Oakland on August 29 and was lost near San Bernardino County.

hardware.title: Tau Robotics' teleoperated humanoid cleaned a reporter's apartment while logging human-piloted motions as training data for future autonomy
hardware.summary: Tau's 4.5-foot robots are piloted remotely over head and wrist cameras and use 3D-printed claws, so the company has done only a couple hundred cleanings, though it claims vacuuming and mopping already run autonomously.

hardware.title: The Trump administration is reportedly weighing four sealed-pod underwater data centers off Maine and Alaska, building on Microsoft's test that saw 87% fewer server failures
hardware.summary: Submerging sealed pods could cut cooling costs and sidestep the community opposition that land sites face.
